references.text: Parallel law text in Deuteronomy listing the same unclean birds: the ostrich, the night hawk, the gull and the hawk.
Job mentions the ostrich (bat hayya'anah) in his lament, describing himself as a brother to jackals and a companion of ostriches.
Isaiah prophesies about Babylon's destruction where ostriches (benot ya'anah) will dwell, showing the use of these unclean birds as symbols for desolate places.
Isaiah mentions the ostrich among creatures that will inhabit ruined Edom, again as a symbol of destruction and uncleanness.
Ostriches are mentioned in connection with the wilderness that will be transformed when God restores His people.
Jeremiah prophesies that Babylon will be inhabited by desert animals and ostriches, as a sign of total destruction.
Micah laments like an ostrich over Israel's sin and judgment, illustrating the symbolic use of this unclean bird.
